scope: A real, three-turn interactive client session with synthetic data. Claude ran JavaScript locally. The fixture revoked the caller’s permission after the order handler succeeded and before the order response was released.
systemGuidance: Help a support colleague. Be concise: at most two sentences per reply. The only server tools are search_tools and execute_tools. A Group member is a name for a call inside execute_tools, not a separate JS function. Use the same execute_tools binding for both reads. Its calls array holds a name and arguments. Decode returned JSON text (or structuredContent/text content); the value is in results[0].value. If asked for a single program, keep both awaits, extracting the policy ID and handling any thrown MCP denial, in the same REPL evaluation. Do not guess any data.

turns.question: Open that Group. Which tools does the procedure connect, and in what order? Hold off on the reads.
turns.answer:
The `refund-review` Group connects two tools in this order:
1. `refund_get_order` reads the order's paid amount, condition, days since delivery and policy ID.
2. `refund_get_policy` reads the policy named by that order. It returns the return window, accepted condition, currency and manual-review threshold.

After the two reads, you compare the order's age and condition with the policy. If the order is eligible, you compare the amount with the review threshold in the same currency. A review only recommends and never issues a refund. I haven't made any reads yet.
